---
title: "Architecture reference"
---

## Runtime discovery

`MethodMeshApplication` discovers module objects at startup and installs them into `MethodMeshModuleRegistry`. The registry asserts uniqueness of module IDs, method IDs, capability-screen IDs and shared Settings-section IDs before installing methods into the runtime method registry.

## Core + module methods

Discovered modules contribute their own `As100Method` lists. The shared runtime additionally contributes scheduler create/export/import methods and screens. This is one reason documentation should distinguish module capabilities from shared runtime facilities.

## Module contract surface

A `MethodMeshModule` may expose:

- `moduleId`, `displayName`, `summary`, `iconKey`;
- `as100Methods()`;
- `rilBindings()`;
- `capabilityScreens()`;
- `capabilitySettings()`;
- shared `settingsSections()` where genuinely module-owned;
- module dependencies;
- examples.

## Discovery, not a hand-written central list

Adding a capability should not require teaching dashboard/shared UI about its internals. The module advertises generic metadata; shared surfaces render/project that metadata.

## Transport architecture

ODK/Android return projection, namespace handling, binary grants and full-JSON formatting belong to shared transport code. Capability modules declare outputs; they do not maintain a separate ODK result model.
